project_scope: QuranHikma Tafsir only; separate from Global Equb
action: Compared the opening attribution clause in the live Arabic and English rows with two digital Arabic Qurtubi witnesses and classified only the voice/route stated by this sentence.

source_anchors.source: QKS Qurani KSU Qurtubi electronic witness
source_anchors.locator: Sūrah 108 opening, electronic page label 602, lines 23–25
source_anchors.finding: The opening says the surah is Meccan in the named authorities' view, then states that it has three verses; it does not present a direct quotation from any named authority or an oral chain here.

source_anchors.source: Quranpedia Qurtubi, al-Jamiʿ li-ahkam al-Qurʾan, 2nd edition
source_anchors.locator: Sūrah 108 introduction, displayed print page 216; edition metadata lines 9–23
source_anchors.finding: The full edition separates the opening Makki attribution from a distinct following Medinan-opinion clause. This confirms the opinion-list structure in that displayed edition; it does not supply an oral chain for the opening statement.

source_anchors.locator: public.tafsir_entries rows 13239 Arabic and 38030 English, Sūrah 108:1
source_anchors.finding: Arabic contains the Makki list including Muqatil; paired English currently gives Mujahid in that list. Neither row's source_url value is an edition locator.

voice_assessment.direct_observation: The Arabic clause marks the Makki characterization as a view attributed to named authorities; the phrase is followed by a separate verse-count statement.
voice_assessment.inference: This opening functions as Qurtubi's reported attribution of a view, rather than a direct quotation or a claim that Qurtubi personally prefers this view. The syntax by itself does not establish the authorities' individual source routes.
voice_assessment.chain_status: No oral transmission chain is stated in this opening clause. Do not infer or append one.
voice_assessment.rejected_view_status: No rejected view appears in this bounded opening clause; the separate Medinan opinion in the fuller edition remains a distinct opinion unit and is absent from the live Arabic row.
